subject: science
skillName: States of Matter and Particle Motion

items.prompt:
In which state are particles packed tightly and vibrating in place?
A) Gas
B) Liquid
C) Solid
D) None

steps: Solids have tightly packed, vibrating particles.

items.prompt:
In which state are particles far apart and moving quickly?
A) Solid
B) Liquid
C) Gas
D) Frozen

steps: Gas particles are spread out and move fast.

items.prompt:
Adding thermal energy makes particles:
A) Move slower
B) Move faster
C) Stop
D) Disappear

Which state has particles that are close together but can slide past one another?
A) Solid
B) Liquid
C) Gas
D) Plasma

steps: Liquid particles stay close but can move past each other.

items.prompt:
Heating ice until it melts changes it from a solid to a:
A) Gas
B) Liquid
C) Plasma
D) New element

steps: Melting changes a solid to a liquid.

items.prompt:
Removing thermal energy from a gas can cause it to:
A) Spread out more
B) Condense into a liquid
C) Move faster
D) Become hotter

steps: Cooling slows particles so the gas can condense.

items.prompt:
As heat is added, a substance goes solid -> liquid -> gas because the particles:
A) Slow down and pack tighter
B) Move faster and spread apart
C) Stop moving
D) Turn into atoms
items.answer: B) Move faster and spread apart

steps: Added energy makes particles move faster and spread, changing the state.

items.prompt:
Which correctly ranks the states from lowest to highest particle energy?
A) Gas, liquid, solid
B) Solid, liquid, gas
C) Liquid, solid, gas
D) Gas, solid, liquid

steps: Solids have the least particle energy and gases the most.
